before.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
before.description: The Taycan 12V auxiliary battery drains excessively when the vehicle is parked, even for short periods. The numerous electronic modules and always-on connectivity features draw more current than the 12V battery management system can sustain. A dead 12V battery prevents the car from powering on even with a full high-voltage battery.
before.solution: Update to the latest Porsche software version which includes improved 12V battery management. Replace the 12V battery with an AGM unit if degraded. Install a 12V battery maintainer for extended parking. Disable unnecessary always-on features in the vehicle settings.

before.title: Air Suspension Strut Retaining Ring Dislodgement (Air Spring Strut Failure)
before.description: An incorrectly machined groove in the support-bearing area of the air spring strut can cause the retaining ring to seat improperly. The ring can come loose, allowing the strut to become dislodged and air to escape from the air spring. The vehicle then drops on one corner, an air-suspension warning appears, and handling/control can be compromised. Documented on air-suspension-equipped early Taycans (and the sister Audi e-tron GT) via a US recall; German owners have reported similar low-volume cases on motor-talk.de.
before.solution: Recall/repair remedy: dealers inspect and replace the affected air spring strut(s) where the retaining-ring groove is out of spec, free of charge under the campaign. Owners noticing the car sitting low on one corner with a suspension warning should stop driving and have it inspected before further use.
symptoms: Vehicle lowers/sags on one corner
Air suspension warning message in instrument cluster
Audible air leak from a strut
Degraded ride height and handling

before.title: Charge Port Door (Power Supply Flap) Actuator Failure / Cross-Lock Fault
before.description: The electrically actuated charge port doors (power supply flaps) commonly fail to open or close, or get stuck halfway, preventing charging. Because the Taycan uses a 'cross-lock' safety function that locks the opposite flap whenever one is opened, a fault on one side can produce a misleading error message for the other side, making diagnosis confusing. Owners report this across model years from 2020 onward; failures are typically the flap actuator motor, wiring, or module.
before.solution: Porsche addressed it via TSB 186/24 and workshop campaign WLK2 (covered by a later TSB dated April 7, 2025): dealers replace the failed actuator, repair wiring, or replace the entire flap module as needed. As a temporary workaround, lock the car, move the key fob at least ~30 feet away, and wait 15-20 minutes to let the systems reset, which can restore flap function. Out-of-warranty actuator/module replacement typically runs a few hundred dollars in parts plus labor.
symptoms: Charge port door won't open or close
Flap stuck halfway
Error message references the wrong (opposite) side due to cross-lock
Unable to charge

before.title: Front Brake Hose Cracking and Brake Fluid Leak
before.description: The front brake hoses can become over-stressed at their point of minimum bending radius during certain steering and driving conditions, damaging the inner fabric liner. Over time the hose can crack and leak brake fluid, dropping hydraulic pressure at the front axle, extending stopping distances and degrading braking in extreme cases. Production cars built after May 13, 2024 received revised hoses with a larger bending radius.
before.solution: Recall remedy (NHTSA 24V-455 / Porsche ARB0): dealers replace the front brake hoses with revised hoses that have an increased bending radius, free of charge. Owners seeing 'brake fluid low' or 'PSM failure' messages should stop driving and have the vehicle inspected.

before.title: Front Passenger Airbag Deactivation (Occupant Classification System / Seat Heating Mat Crimp Defect)
before.description: A manufacturing defect in the crimp connection of the front passenger seat cushion's heating mat can cause the Occupant Classification System (OCS) to malfunction and enter a fail-safe mode, deactivating the front passenger airbag even when the seat is occupied. Owners who see the 'Passenger Airbag OFF' light illuminated with an occupant in the seat should treat it as the defect symptom and get it inspected.

before.title: High-Voltage Battery Internal Short-Circuit and Fire Risk (LG Module Defect)
before.description: A supplier manufacturing defect in certain LG-built lithium-ion battery modules (assembled in Poland) can cause internal damage that develops into a short circuit within the high-voltage pack. There is no early warning to the driver, and in the worst case the short can trigger a thermal event or fire. This is a safety/fire-risk defect separate from the gradual capacity/range loss owners also report. Porsche issued an interim instruction to limit charging to 80 percent state of charge until the fix was available.
before.solution: Recall remedy (NHTSA 24V-732 / Porsche ARB6/ARB7, which superseded earlier campaigns 23V-840, 24V-215, 24V-217): dealers install advanced battery-monitoring diagnostic software that continuously watches for patterns of internal damage, and replace individually affected cell modules — or the entire pack where flagged — free of charge. Owners were told to charge only to 80% until the diagnostic software/repair was applied.
symptoms: No early warning before failure
Battery-related warning messages
Charging limited to 80% per Porsche advisory
Potential thermal event or fire in rare cases

before.title: Onboard AC Charger (22 kW Option) Failure - 'Electrical System Fault'
before.description: The optional 22 kW onboard AC charger (OBC) is prone to failure. When it fails the car throws a yellow 'Electrical System Fault' warning and, in some cases, the car will not move at all; AC (Level 2) charging stops working. Porsche reportedly cannot reliably supply replacement 22 kW units and has discontinued the option, so it offers owners compensation (~€1,700-€1,800) to downgrade to the more reliable 11 kW charger. Out-of-warranty replacement of the original unit is very expensive.
before.solution: Under warranty (including Porsche Approved Warranty), the OBC is replaced as a warranty claim. Because 22 kW units are scarce, Porsche commonly offers a goodwill payment (~€1,700) to downgrade to the stable 11 kW charger, which dealers note rarely fails. Out of warranty, a replacement can run roughly $7,000-$10,000 depending on dealer, making the 11 kW downgrade the practical fix.

before.title: High-Voltage Battery Range Degradation
before.description: Some Taycan owners report faster-than-expected range degradation, particularly in cold climates and after frequent DC fast charging. The battery management system may also display inconsistent range estimates. While some degradation is normal for lithium-ion batteries, rates exceeding 5% per year are considered above normal.
before.solution: Have the battery health checked at a Porsche dealer using PIWIS diagnostics. Minimize DC fast charging to 80% and prefer AC home charging. Avoid storing the vehicle at very high or very low states of charge. Porsche provides an 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranty covering capacity loss below 70%.

proposal.title: High-Voltage Battery Range Degradation

Do not buy a battery pack, cell module, charger or diagnostic device from this page; measured capacity, fault identity, warranty terms, current part number and VIN applicability must be established first.

before.title: Sudden Powertrain Shutdown / Total Loss of Power While Driving (Pulse Inverter Software)
before.description: A software fault in the pulse-control inverter / power electronics and motor control unit can incorrectly detect a fault and trigger a complete shutdown of the powertrain while the car is in motion. The driver gets a warning such as 'Motor control error - Stop vehicle in a safe place' and the car coasts to a stop with no drive power; steering and brakes remain. This is a high crash risk in highway or passing situations. Affected roughly 43,000 cars globally.
before.solution: Recall remedy (NHTSA 21V-486 / Porsche campaign AMB5): dealers reprogram the power electronics / motor control software so a false error message no longer triggers a full powertrain shutdown. The update is free and takes about an hour in the workshop.
symptoms: Warning 'Motor control error - Stop vehicle in a safe place'
Sudden complete loss of motive power
Car coasts to a stop
Acceleration lost while steering and brakes remain

before.title: Front Suspension Clunking and Creaking
before.description: The Taycan front suspension produces clunking and creaking noises over bumps and during low-speed maneuvering. The issue is traced to the upper strut mounts, control arm bushings, and anti-roll bar end links. The heavy battery pack places additional stress on the front suspension components, accelerating wear.
before.solution: Replace worn upper strut mounts, control arm bushings, or anti-roll bar end links. Porsche has released updated parts with improved durability. Lubricate suspension contact points with silicone-based lubricant as a temporary measure.
symptoms: Clunking over bumps
Creaking during low-speed turns
Rattling from front suspension area
Noise worse in cold weather
Steering wheel vibration over rough surfaces

communityRecommendations.content: Have the front anti-roll bar end links checked first — they are the most common source of the clunking noise and the cheapest component to replace.

proposal.title: Front Suspension Clunking and Creaking
proposal.description: The complete 7,691-row Taycan corpus contains no Porsche communication establishing the frozen 2020-2025 front clunk-and-creak identity or attributing it to upper strut mounts, control-arm bushings and anti-roll-bar links as one recurring failure. The term-matched records instead describe separate conditions such as lower-control-arm grease traces, footwell or body creaks, brake-actuation noise and a VIN-bounded strut retaining-ring recall. None proves battery-weight-accelerated wear, updated universal parts or silicone lubrication as a remedy. The frozen owner total is not a manufacturer-report count.
proposal.solution: Record the exact sound, corner, temperature, steering angle, brake input, road input and speed, then reproduce it with chassis ears or loaded inspection. Check fastener torque, wheel and brake paths, control arms, links, mounts, strut, air-suspension pressure, body joints and steering separately under the model-specific procedure. Check VIN recall status without assuming recall identity from noise alone. Do not buy a strut mount, control arm, bushing, end link, air strut or lubricant from this page; the noise source, failed component, current part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
